construct: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency prevents normal cleavage of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers, allowing highly platelet-adhesive VWF multimers to accumulate on endothelium and form platelet-rich microthrombi that cause thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, and ischemic organ dysfunction.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency causes failure to cleave ultra-large VWF, platelet-rich microthrombi, platelet consumption, schistocytic hemolysis, and neurologic ischemia.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: The complement-mediated aHUS option is a genuine thrombotic-microangiopathy alternative, but ADAMTS13 activity below 10% plus the specified VWF-cleavage mechanism uniquely supports TTP. The VWF-factor-VIII, fibrinolysis, and GPIIb/IIIa options produce bleeding/fibrinolytic phenotypes rather than ADAMTS13-deficient platelet-rich microthrombi.
